summary: The shipping-once major is closed. `completesOrder` now uses the same coverage rule as `cancelShare` (cancelled or holding a live claim, with FAILED excluded). So a return requested while a sibling cancel is REQUESTED is completing and carries the shipping. The frozen cancel stays non-completing, and `shippingAlreadyRefunded` stops any second carrier. The new IT proves this. The extended guard (FAILED and `shippingAlreadyRefunded()`) is precise. A FAILED shipment holds no claim and, being pre-dispatch, has no return. So any live claim or non-rejected return that carries shipping can only have completed because this shipment was covered while it was REQUESTED, and the guard never blocks a ship that the money did not depend on. The exit path still works: a retry re-freezes the shipment as the remainder with shipping already taken, and the runbook now has the return variant of the query. The `fullyRefunded` change is correct. It counts only DONE cancels, so no money is assumed for REQUESTED claims, and it requires every return to be REFUNDED or REJECTED. `commitCancel` evaluates it after the shipment is marked CANCELLED, so the cancel and return paths now set REFUNDED the same way, and the all-shipments-cancelled case behaves as before. The B3 backlog entries are in backlog.md. Remaining items are a minor test gap (the return arm of the guard) and a nit. The approval assumes the CEO records V-ALL and forge-verify for the stacked head before the gate, and that A and B merge together.
